text:
What do you capture, nocturnal, in your songs, foolish Góngora, by twilighting them, if when you most yearn to heron-flight them, you reptilize and underpose them more?

God microcosmed you with inquisitions, and you want them to investigate you by medals as ancient signs or antiquities, to unroute apprentice bards.

Your foreignness is so eminent that whoever ruminates you must detract you, for you belch visceral cacochymy,

pharmaco-coloring like a mummy, if you give such slight stomach-abundance, metamorphosing arcadumy.

Yesterday was a dream; tomorrow will be earth! A moment before, nothing; a moment after, smoke! I assign ambitions and presume scarcely a point within the circle closing me!

Brief combat of troublesome war: in my defense I am the greatest danger; while my weapons consume me, the body lodges me less than buries me.

Yesterday is gone; tomorrow has not arrived; today passes, is, and was, in a motion hurling me toward death.

Hour and instant are spades that, paid by my pain and care, dig my monument in my life.

translation.title: What Do You Capture, Nocturnal, in Your Songs?
